clue.text: Piece of music in Swan Lake perhaps shortly captivating those attending

indicators.note: captivating means holding something inside, so one piece goes within the other
shortly says the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: Swan Lake is an example of a ballet
the gate is the crowd attending a sporting event

explanation.surface: A short musical number is performed in a ballet and charms the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swan Lake perhaps' defines by example, and 'those attending' is the crowd at a match, not people at the ballet.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagatelle is a short light composition, typically for piano.

clue.text: Soldiers once rise into cloud

parts.note: the BEF, British Expeditionary Force, was the army sent to France in both world wars
to rise is to go up, so in a down clue the word go is written upwards

explanation.surface: Old troops climb up into the clouds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' is a link. 'rise' gives 'go up', which in a down answer means GO written bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: To befog is to envelop in mist, so cloud as a verb means the same, literally or figuratively.

clue.text: Torquemada's relative, corruptly quids in, one going to rise

definitions.note: the possessive reads as 'Torquemada is', the man being named

parts.note: a gran is a grandmother, a relative

indicators.note: corruptly says the letters are put into a corrupted order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a tor is a rocky hill, a rise in the land

explanation.surface: Torquemada's kinsman is in profit by foul means and rising in the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corruptly' rearranges QUIDSIN to DINQUIS; 'going to' is a link. Torquemada headed the Spanish Inquisition, so 'Torquemada's' reads as 'Torquemada is' the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomas de Torquemada was the first Grand Inquisitor of the Spanish Inquisition, so the title names him.

clue.text: Surface, given medication before surgery

indicators.note: before puts the medication ahead of the surgery in the answer

parts.note: a tablet is a pill, a dose of medication
op is short for operation, surgery

explanation.surface: A patient is given a pill before an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabletop is the flat upper surface of a table.

clue.text: Poet's abandoned the turf, some say

indicators.note: some say signals a word that sounds like another in speech

parts.note: a lawn is an area of turf

explanation.surface: A poet laments a neglected lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the two words sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorn is an old poetic word for forsaken or desolate, so it suits a poet's 'abandoned'.

clue.text: Westminster guide before spring receiving envelope

indicators.note: receiving means taking another piece inside

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
a skin is an outer covering, an envelope
May is a month of spring

explanation.surface: A parliamentary handbook arrives in its envelope ahead of the spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' puts SKIN inside ERE. ERSKINE MAY is the standard guide to procedure in the UK Parliament at Westminster.
explanation.definitionFit: Erskine May is the reference book on parliamentary procedure used at Westminster.

clue.text: That is flax, that thing

parts.note: tow is the coarse broken fibre of flax
it is the pronoun for that thing

explanation.surface: Someone points out a bundle of flax.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a formal way of saying namely, introducing an explanation.

clue.text: Roof given a particular check

parts.note: that points to a particular one
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: A roof is given a specific inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatch is a roof covering of straw or reeds, and the word also means to roof with it.

clue.text: Swallowed arrant nonsense as description of conflict with Kaiser?

indicators.note: nonsense says the letters are turned into a jumble before being sorted

explanation.surface: Someone accepted utter rubbish about a war with the German emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonsense' rearranges SWALLOWEDARRANT; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase was the optimistic slogan for the First World War, fought against the Kaiser's Germany.

clue.text: One starting book has to chuck it over senility?

indicators.note: over says the pieces are turned to read the other way

parts.note: to pelt is to throw, chuck
age here is old age, the time of senility

explanation.surface: Someone must throw an item over because of old age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns PELTIT into TITLEP. 'has to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The title page is the leaf at the start of a book giving its title and author.

clue.text: Novel in four parts Albert translated

indicators.note: translated means turned into another form, here a new order of letters

explanation.surface: A novel in four sections has been translated by a man named Albert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges FOURPARTSALBERT. Julian Barnes's 1984 novel takes its name from the stuffed bird Flaubert kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Julian Barnes wrote this 1984 novel about a stuffed bird linked to the French writer.

clue.text: Heartlessly saw into great device

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Gt is the abbreviation for great, as in Gt Britain

indicators.note: heartlessly says the middle letter is taken away

parts.note: a saw is an old saying, an adage

explanation.surface: Someone cruelly put a saw into a fine machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' is the old saying, not the tool; 'great' is the abbreviation seen in Gt Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadget is a small mechanical device or tool.

clue.text: Betray one's class, breaking into ration

indicators.note: breaking into says one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a dose is a measured ration of medicine
one's gives I (one) with S
CL is the abbreviation for class

explanation.surface: Someone betrays their social class by raiding the rations.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclose is to reveal a secret, which can mean betraying it.

clue.text: Not made to stay at home in the dark

indicators.note: to stay says one piece is kept inside the other

parts.note: unformed means not yet made or shaped
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone not forced to stay at home is kept in ignorance.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the dark is an idiom for lacking information.

clue.text: Surprised by ending of Te Deum?

definitions.meaning: the hymn's last line asks 'let me never be' this word

explanation.surface: Someone is startled by how a hymn ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The Te Deum closes 'O Lord, in thee have I trusted: let me never be confounded'; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Confounded means bewildered or taken aback, a close synonym of surprised.

clue.text: The cap's on? Wrong, at these

definitions.text: The cap's on? Wrong, at these

indicators.note: wrong says the letters are set the wrong way and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Keeping one's hat on at a war memorial is a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' rearranges THECAPSON. The whole clue defines: at war memorials men take caps off.
explanation.definitionFit: Cenotaphs are war memorials, at which men traditionally remove their hats.

clue.text: Old American almost preserved

indicators.note: almost says the last letter is left off

parts.note: food that is preserved is in a can

explanation.surface: An elderly American is nearly embalmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of INCAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas were the native people of the Andean empire conquered by Spain.

clue.text: Weapon, as I recall, really is fast loading: excellent at the front

indicators.note: at the front points to the opening letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a gun that is quick and excellent to load.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon is punctuation; the letters run from 'as' to 'excellent'. 'excellent at the front' looks like A1 heading the answer, but it is the selection signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An air rifle is a gun firing pellets by compressed air, a kind of weapon.

clue.text: Word number one, overseas

parts.note: un is French for one

explanation.surface: The first item on a list is abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun is a kind of word, a naming word in grammar.

clue.text: Disprove hospital report of returning appetite?

definitions.meaning: read as two words it says a sick patient has eaten

explanation.surface: A hospital bulletin says a patient is hungry again.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as INVALID ATE, the answer is a ward note that the patient has eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To invalidate an argument is to show it is unsound, to disprove it.

clue.text: King shrewd about where sea and ocean end?

indicators.note: about says one piece goes round the other

parts.note: cute can mean clever or shrewd

indicators.note: end points to the final letter of each word

explanation.surface: A wise king knows where the sea stops.
explanation.walkthrough: King Canute famously sat on the shore to show his courtiers he could not stop the tide, hence the sea's edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Canute (Cnut) was an 11th-century king of England, Denmark and Norway.

clue.text: To run over property briefly, one may need solicitor

indicators.note: over says the outer pieces lie across, enclosing the other

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: briefly says the last letter is cut off

parts.note: an estate is a property
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone checks over a property quickly and needs a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the end: a person making a will may need a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is a person making a will, who would usually employ a solicitor to draw it up.

clue.text: French gendarmerie kicking out extremists for fun

indicators.note: kicking out extremists says the first and last letters are thrown out

parts.note: the gendarmerie is a police force

explanation.surface: French police throw out some extremists for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kicking out extremists' takes the first and last letters off POLICE, leaving OLIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A frolic is lively playful fun or a merry outing.

clue.text: Value a place for cheap holiday

parts.note: the cost of something is its value

explanation.surface: Someone weighs the cost of a budget break.
explanation.walkthrough: A costa is a Spanish coast, such as the Costa del Sol, popular for package holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish coastal resorts such as the Costa Brava are classic destinations for cheap package holidays.

clue.text: God is interested? Not at first

indicators.note: not at first says the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: one who cares is interested

explanation.surface: Is God interested? Not initially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not at first' drops the C from CARES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ares was the Greek god of war.

clue.text: Given further insults, loses heart for book

parts.note: someone given more insults is put out more, more offended
to flag is to tire or lose heart

explanation.surface: Insulted again and again, someone loses heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link. The book is Evelyn Waugh's 1942 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a 1942 novel by Evelyn Waugh.

clue.text: Help get game started

definitions.meaning: to assist or be of use to
in tennis the opening stroke starts play

explanation.surface: A helper starts a game.
explanation.definitionFit: To serve is to help, and in tennis the serve begins each point.

clue.text: Pepys said to suffer from this?

definitions.text: Pepys said to suffer from this?

indicators.note: to suffer suggests the letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Samuel Pepys is reported to have had an ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to suffer' rearranges PEPYSSAID. Pepys was a diarist famous for recording his dinners.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspepsia is indigestion, a complaint a hearty eater might suffer from.
